$comment: Which hermetic test files run on every pull request and in `bun run test:macos` (the essential tier), and which only in the weekly full run. A file in a slow category is essential only when it is listed below (at most 3 per category; a new file there is weekly until it is listed). Any other file is essential unless ci-test-times.json measures it at heavySeconds or more. ci-tests.ts reads this file; ai-docs/architecture/testing.md explains how to promote a file.

essential.guards: a real pane session starts, answers and settles COMPLETED through this tree's claudish; CLAUDISH_PANE_CHILD is kept in the child; a nested --team is refused with exit 64; nothing outlives the reap
only the read-only magmux-<id>.view socket is verified and published, it refuses input, and the reap removes it with no orphan
HERDR_* and the five HC_* identities are stripped from the pane and replay environments while the nesting marker stays; contract v1 capability order
the real MCP server, started directly, through a launcher pair and through the npm launcher (bin/claudish.cjs → dist), records hostPid/launcherPid/mcpPid in spawn.json, with no pane left behind
SessionManager starts real pane sessions: a caller session id, the artifact directory, and the child's own CLAUDISH_TOKEN_FILE and upstream-error log reach the child
session records and Claude Code's config directory follow a runtime HOME, so claudish never writes the account home while the monitor reads a sandbox
the exact 20-tool surface, and the 4-tool nested mode that keeps create_session out of a session
create_session, send_input, get_output, cancel_session and list_sessions end to end through the real MCP server and real panes, with no orphan

run_prompt on a Claude model through the real MCP server: the one print child the server starts gets its exact argv, a stripped auth/session/pane environment and an empty cwd, and its errors reach the caller
a settled slot is judged by its answer, not its exit code: api_error, prompt_not_read, refused, empty_output and shape_mismatch in precedence order
a team run on real panes settles and its answer, read from the transcript, reaches response-<id>.md byte-exact
a run that fails to start stops every pane already started, a SIGTERM-ignoring slot included, so nothing keeps billing
a connection failure never advances the routing chain, so an outage cannot move a subscription user onto a metered hop
an exhausted network fault answers 400 connection_error, never an auth or rate-limit status, even after an earlier hop's 401
a request that recovers mid-ladder completes with its body and credential intact, so a retry never turns an outage into a 401
the response seam: intercept and buffer modes, fail-open, client cancel, the observe tap and the non-streaming branch
with hooks loaded, nothing but JSON-RPC reaches the MCP server's stdout
the hook chain: closed actions, the circuit breaker, journal fan-out and pending notes
